newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse lags neighbours, seen drifting.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse lags neighbours, seen drifting.

text.p: The Brussels bourse lagged its European neighbours on their upwards march on Monday, and traders said the holiday-hit market was likely to drift in coming days in the absence of major news.
"It was really disappointing given the rest of Europe and the level of the dollar, especially considering that in Belgium we have a lot of dollar sensitive companies," one trader said.
"The only reason is that the holidays have now really started and most people are away for the next couple of weeks," he added.
However, there were still some star performers that stood out from the general lacklustre tone of the market.
Chief among these was chemicals and pharmaceutical firm UCB , which ended 4.8 percent higher at 135,200 francs having at one stage hit a new year high of 136,400 francs.
Traders said the rise in a quiet market was the result of very aggressive buying by a few players. They could give no specific reason.
"There is no company news, but most people expect UCB to report good first half figures at the end of the month," one trader said.

Another strong performer was electronics firm Barco , which added 1.6 percent to 7,610 francs on positive follow-through sentiment after the firm announced late on Friday it had bought Danish audio and video firm RE.
Generale Bank, which upgraded the stock to buy from hold following an analysts meeting on Friday, said that while the purchase would not impact sales significantly it would be profitable.

The Bel-20 index of blue-chip shares .BFX ended the day 8.91 points or 0.36 percent higher at 2,501.32, with seven gainers, two unchanged and 11 losers. Just over two billion francs worth of Belgian shares changed hands out of a total market volume of 3.8 billion francs.
